== Biography ==

The Dormouse is a creature best described as perpetually asleep. At the tea party beneath the tree, it sat nestled between the March Hare and the Hatter, where the two used it as a comfortable cushion, resting their elbows upon it as they talked over its head. Yet despite its slumber, the Dormouse would speak—replies emerging from its sleep in the curious logic of dreams. When the March Hare claimed that "I like what I get" is the same as "I get what I like," the Dormouse answered (still sleeping) that "I breathe when I sleep" is equally the same as "I sleep when I breathe." The creature also sang whilst asleep, though a pinch from its companions was required to bring the singing to an end.

The Dormouse attended the trial alongside the March Hare. There, it answered "Sixteenth" to a question about a date. Seated beside Alice during the trial, it complained of her proximity: "I wish you wouldn't squeeze so. I can hardly breathe."

== Relationships ==

'''[[March Hare]]''' — acquaintance. At the tea party, the Dormouse sits between the March Hare and Hatter, who use it as a cushion. The two share wordplay and conversation, remaining together at trial.

'''[[Alice]]''' — acquaintance. Alice encounters the Dormouse at the tea party and again at trial. At trial, when Alice sits adjacent to the Dormouse, it protests against the crowding.

'''[[Hatter]]''' — acquaintance. The Hatter is the Dormouse's companion at the tea party, using it as a cushion and engaging it in conversation. Both later appear together at trial.

'''[[Queen]]''' — The Dormouse seems to incur the Queen's displeasure when it sings in its sleep at the tea party; the Queen's outburst suggests the Dormouse is viewed unfavorably.
